context: Hiroshi-elder teaches Sho-young how to fly a kite at the park.
purpose: Grandfather sharing classic childhood activity with grandson.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 凧、風、ようけ吹いとるな。
lines.en: That wind's really picking up, isn't it.
lines.style: Measured, almost dreamy observation. Slow Kansai cadence. Warm affection in the tone—watching both kite and child. Small smile in the voice.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.style: Sharp intake of breath on the first word. Voice cracks with genuine wonder. Quick, bright delivery. Absolute awe—the kind a six-year-old can't fake.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ようやった、お前、上手や!
lines.en: You did well—you're good at this.
lines.style: Soft, genuine praise. Light tap on 「上手」—quiet conviction, not overplaying it. Kansai warmth underneath. The voice of someone proud without needing to say it loudly.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.en: The sky's almost swallowing it up.
lines.style: Breathless wonder. Voice rises slightly with the kite. Fast, excited delivery—infectious childhood excitement. Small laugh tucked underneath.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.en: Being with you like this—it's really something.
lines.style: Long, contented exhale. Kansai lilt on the trailing syllables. Slow pace, unhurried. Deep fondness in every word. The voice of someone fully present in a moment he knows matters.
